clue.text: Greeting not so sensible when received by fool with nothing on

indicators.note: one piece is received, taken in, by the other piece, so it sits inside it

parts.note: a goon is a fool, a stupid person
dafter is the comparative of daft, silly, so less sensible
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone says hello less wisely after being taken in by a naked idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard salutation used between noon and evening, so it is a greeting.

clue.text: Transports writer into sources of inspiration led by love

indicators.note: being led by something means it comes in front, so this piece goes first

parts.note: love is nil in tennis scoring, written O

indicators.note: into says the writer piece is put inside the sources piece

parts.note: the Muses are the Greek goddesses who inspire the arts
a nib is the writing point of a pen, so a writer

explanation.surface: A writer is carried away by the Muses and by love, a romantic picture of creative rapture.
explanation.definitionFit: Buses that carry passengers are vehicles, so the plural noun means means of transport.

clue.text: Game with neighbours at 14

definitions.meaning: a local ... is a match between teams from neighbouring places
the classic horse race run at Epsom, the answer to 14 across

explanation.definitionFit: Both the local football fixture and the Epsom classic race carry this same name.

clue.text: Analyst entering right into long-standing quarrel

indicators.note: into says the right piece is put inside the quarrel piece

parts.note: a feud is a bitter quarrel lasting a long time

explanation.surface: A therapist steps right into the middle of an old family row.
explanation.definitionFit: Sigmund Freud founded psychoanalysis, so he is the archetypal analyst.

clue.text: Result of a tongue-tied journalist missing restaurant experience

indicators.note: result of says the letters that follow are rearranged to produce something new
missing says the journalist letters are taken away from the fodder

parts.note: ED, short for editor, is the crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter who cannot get the words out misses out on a night at a restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove ED from the end of ATONGUETIED to leave ATONGUETI, and 'Result of' rearranges those nine letters. 'Tongue-tied' looks like a description but is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Dining at a restaurant rather than at home is the experience of having a meal away.

clue.text: Commercial opportunity opening up, of course

definitions.meaning: a fresh sector or region in which to sell goods
a racecourse, here the famous one in Suffolk

explanation.definitionFit: A fresh outlet for trade is a new market, and Newmarket is the Suffolk racecourse town.

clue.text: God is taking part of poet

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A deity is said to take on a role as a verse writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who writes odes is a kind of poet.

clue.text: Salisbury home used half the 10 when repaired

indicators.note: something repaired is put back together, so these letters are reassembled

parts.note: the figures 1 and 0 read as the letters I and O

explanation.surface: A stately house where half of some earlier thing was put to use once mended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The 10' looks like a cross-reference to 10 across but stands for the letters IO. Add these to USEDHALFTHE and 'repaired' rearranges all thirteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Hatfield House in Hertfordshire is the ancestral seat of the Marquesses of Salisbury.

clue.text: Permit a month at Italian resort when I leave a mysterious isle

parts.note: DEC is the short form of December

indicators.note: leave says the letter I departs from the resort word

parts.note: Rimini is a seaside resort on Italy's Adriatic coast

indicators.note: mysterious says the following letters are muddled into a new order

explanation.surface: Holiday plans: December in Rimini, then off to some enigmatic island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' is a link word. 'mysterious' rearranges A and ISLE to give ALISE.
explanation.definitionFit: To decriminalise something is to make it legal, to permit what was banned.

clue.text: One among the leaves, of course

parts.note: A means one, as in a single thing
in means among
a tree is the thing that bears leaves

explanation.surface: A single item lies somewhere in a pile of foliage.
explanation.walkthrough: In this puzzle 'of course' defines a racecourse; Aintree near Liverpool hosts the Grand National.
explanation.definitionFit: Aintree is the racecourse near Liverpool, so it is one of the puzzle's courses.

clue.text: Remain in the reclaimed land

indicators.note: in says the remain piece sits inside the word the

parts.note: to wait is to remain where one is

explanation.surface: An instruction to stay put on land won back from the wild.
explanation.walkthrough: THWAITE is an old northern English word, common in place names, for a clearing or land taken into cultivation.
explanation.definitionFit: A dialect word for a meadow or plot cleared and brought into use, so ground reclaimed.

clue.text: Jolly good books piercing the spirit

indicators.note: piercing says the books piece goes right inside the spirit piece

parts.note: a fay is a fairy, a spirit
B is book, so BB is books

explanation.surface: Great news: some volumes have run through a ghost.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabby is British slang for fabulous, an exclamation of approval like splendid.

clue.text: Base of bed able to be pushed around, of course

indicators.note: the base of a down word is its last letter, here of bed

parts.note: furniture on a caster, a small wheel, can be pushed about

explanation.surface: The foot of a bed is wheeled so it can be moved about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' defines a racecourse; Doncaster in Yorkshire runs the St Leger.
explanation.definitionFit: Doncaster is the Yorkshire town whose racecourse stages the St Leger.

clue.text: Records to order, of course

parts.note: EPs are extended-play records
OM stands for the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: Records are produced on demand, naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: Epsom in Surrey is the racecourse where the Derby is run.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsom Downs in Surrey is a racecourse, home of the Derby and the Oaks.

clue.text: Item of small arms as distress signal

parts.note: minute means very small
a gun is an arm, a weapon

explanation.surface: A small firearm used to call for help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Item of' is linking: a gun is one item of arms. The minute gun was fired once a minute by a ship in distress.
explanation.definitionFit: A cannon fired at intervals of a minute was a recognised maritime call for help.

clue.text: Run of the mill residence, say, but capital

parts.note: stock means ordinary, standard

indicators.note: say signals that the residence word is spoken and then spelt as another word

parts.note: home is a residence

explanation.surface: An ordinary house, as it were, yet one of first-rate quality.
explanation.definitionFit: Stockholm is the capital city of Sweden.

clue.text: Maronites arranged for a good press

indicators.note: arranged says the letters of the next word are set in a new order

explanation.surface: A Lebanese Christian community has set things up to get favourable newspaper coverage.
explanation.definitionFit: A steam iron is the appliance that gives clothes a good press.

clue.text: Flower of evening a different one? Just so

indicators.note: arranged just so means put in a particular order, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: other means different

explanation.surface: A bloom that opens at dusk is another sort altogether, exactly so.
explanation.walkthrough: Fodder A, OTHER and ONE is rearranged as signalled by 'Just so'.
explanation.definitionFit: Oenothera is the botanical genus of evening primroses, which open their blooms at dusk.

clue.text: Vice in its place — good guy is to withdraw backing

indicators.note: in places the vice piece inside its place

parts.note: a dive is a seedy bar, the place where vice goes on
a vice is a sin
ST is the abbreviation for saint, a good person

explanation.surface: Vice is put in its place, and a virtuous man pulls out his support.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull investment out of a company or cause is to stop supporting it financially.

clue.text: Main follower in France with projector

definitions.meaning: these letters follow MAIN to make Maintenon, a French town known from Madame de Maintenon
a projecting tongue on the end of a piece of wood, made to fit a mortise

explanation.definitionFit: A tenon is a projecting piece of wood shaped to fit a mortise; Maintenon is a French town.

clue.text: Finished watch — I did more than my share

definitions.text: I did more than my share
definitions.note: the speaker describes themselves as one who works extra hours

parts.note: over means finished
a timer is a watch, a timepiece

explanation.surface: My watch has stopped, and I feel I did more than my bit.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who works beyond the agreed hours does more than their share of the work.

clue.text: Mathematician sounds useful with troubled waters

indicators.note: sounds says the word for the oil-pourer is said and spelt as another

parts.note: an oiler pours oil, and oil is poured on troubled waters to calm them

explanation.surface: A scientist seems handy whenever there is turmoil about.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonhard Euler was an eighteenth-century Swiss mathematician.

clue.text: Fix altitude without mistake

parts.note: to rig is to fix dishonestly, as a result
HT is the abbreviation for height, altitude

explanation.surface: Set the height correctly first time.
explanation.definitionFit: Right means correct, so done with no error.

clue.text: Endearment for model wearing ring?

indicators.note: wearing says one piece is worn inside the other

parts.note: a peal is a ringing of bells
the Model T was Henry Ford's famous car, so model gives T

explanation.surface: A pet name for a fashion model sporting a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Petal is an affectionate term of address, like love or dear.

clue.text: Rose of 17 getting round Levi

parts.note: 17 down is the evening primrose, and the part before rose is these letters
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A flower from another clue winds round a man called Levi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting' is a link word. The definition is a person: the Italian writer Primo Levi.
explanation.definitionFit: Primo Levi was the Italian chemist and writer of If This Is a Man, so the forename identifies him.

clue.text: Broken rest, being interrupted by walker at 13

indicators.note: being interrupted by says another piece breaks into the middle
broken says the letters of rest are smashed and reassembled

parts.note: a leg is what one walks with

explanation.surface: A broken night's sleep, disturbed by someone walking about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broken' turns the second word into STER. In this puzzle 'at 13' points to Doncaster, the Yorkshire course where this classic is run.
explanation.definitionFit: The St Leger is the classic horse race run each September at Doncaster.

clue.text: Be off from dance when at 6

indicators.note: off from says the named letters leave the dance word

parts.note: the beguine is a dance of Caribbean origin
as means when

explanation.surface: Get away from the dance floor when it is six o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at 6' means at Newmarket, where the 1,000 and 2,000 Guineas are run.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1,000 and 2,000 Guineas are classic horse races run at Newmarket.

clue.text: Good and reasonable, with new entry at 10

indicators.note: entry says these letters make their way inside the reasonable word

parts.note: rational means reasonable

explanation.surface: A good and sensible person, with a fresh application to submit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at 10' means at Aintree, where the Grand National steeplechase is run.
explanation.definitionFit: The Grand National is the famous steeplechase run each spring at Aintree.
